name: Cedar Chest
lede: Cedar Chest is a warm reddish orange named for cedar wood, listed in the Crayola range by way of Wikipedia rather than a standards body.

sections.title: A furniture-wood name
sections.body:
Our library's only source for Cedar Chest is Wikipedia, which in turn credits the Crayola crayon line; it carries no Ridgway, ISCC-NBS or Maerz and Paul record[1]. The name points to cedar wood furniture, the kind used to line chests for its scent and insect resistance, rather than to the tree's own bark or foliage color [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[coral-red]], [[dark-coral]], [[dusty-vermilion]] and [[dragon-s-blood]], at 3.8, 3.9, 4 and 5.2 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Cedar Chest in 213 of 23,781 paintings (0.9 percent), as photographed [2]. It is heavily over-represented in paintings from India (3.4 times expected) and especially in the Kalighat school, at 7.4 times its baseline [2]. It most often plays an accent inside a painting, in 89 percent of appearances, and keeps company with [[tussore]] and [[camel]] more than chance [2]. Unlike most names, its earliest archive match, from 1236, does not run ahead of any documented first-recorded year, since Crayola and Wikipedia give none [2].
